{
  "schema": "threatline.threatmodel.v1",
  "issueKey": "EVAL-08",
  "sketch": {
    "components": ["Internal AI agent", "MCP tool discovery/install component", "MCP client runtime", "Installed MCP servers", "Agent tool executor"],
    "dataStores": ["Installed MCP server packages/config"],
    "externalServices": ["Public MCP registry", "Third-party MCP servers"],
    "trustBoundaries": ["Agent runtime <-> public MCP registry", "Agent runtime <-> dynamically installed MCP server", "Untrusted tool output <-> agent reasoning loop"],
    "dataClasses": ["secrets"],
    "exposure": "public",
    "llmFeatures": true
  },
  "threats": [
    {
      "stride": "ElevationOfPrivilege",
      "title": "Malicious MCP server from the public registry runs code inside the agent host",
      "scenario": "An attacker publishes (or typosquats) an MCP server on the public registry. The agent discovers and installs it at runtime, so attacker-controlled package code executes in the agent's process or container with the agent's credentials and network access. No deploy or human review stands in the way, giving the attacker a foothold in the internal environment.",
      "component": "MCP tool discovery/install component",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 5,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "Our internal agent can discover and install new MCP servers from a public registry at runtime so it can use new tools without a deploy." }
      ],
      "asvs": [],
      "cwe": ["CWE-829", "CWE-494", "CWE-1357"],
      "plainLanguage": "The agent downloads and runs software from a public catalogue by itself, so anyone who uploads bad software there can run code on our servers.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Only install MCP servers from a vetted allowlist with verified integrity",
        "given": "the agent wants to use an MCP server that is not already installed",
        "when": "it attempts a runtime discovery and install from the public registry",
        "then": "installation is refused unless the server is on a signed, human-approved allowlist and its artifact signature/digest is verified before execution"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "Tampering",
      "title": "Tool descriptions from installed MCP servers hijack the agent's goal",
      "scenario": "A third-party MCP server returns tool names, descriptions or results containing injected instructions. Because the agent reads these as part of its prompt, the attacker redirects it to exfiltrate data, call other tools or ignore its guardrails (ASI01 goal hijack, ASI06 context poisoning). The attacker needs only to publish a server the agent later installs.",
      "component": "Agent reasoning loop / MCP client runtime",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "AI agent that installs MCP tools" },
        { "quote": "so it can use new tools without a deploy" }
      ],
      "asvs": [],
      "cwe": ["CWE-74"],
      "plainLanguage": "Text that comes back from a newly installed tool can contain hidden orders the agent follows.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Treat MCP metadata and results as untrusted data",
        "given": "an installed MCP server supplies tool descriptions or returns results",
        "when": "that content enters the agent's context",
        "then": "it is wrapped as untrusted data, stripped of instruction-like directives, and cannot alter the agent's system policy or trigger privileged tool calls without fresh authorisation"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "InformationDisclosure",
      "title": "Newly installed tools receive the agent's secrets and internal data",
      "scenario": "A freshly installed MCP server is handed the same credentials, tokens and internal context as trusted tools, and can reach internal services. An attacker-controlled server reads environment secrets or asks the agent to pass internal data as tool arguments, then exfiltrates it to its own endpoint (ASI02/ASI03).",
      "component": "Installed MCP servers",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 5,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "Our internal agent can discover and install new MCP servers from a public registry at runtime" }
      ],
      "asvs": [],
      "cwe": ["CWE-200", "CWE-522"],
      "plainLanguage": "A brand new, unchecked tool gets the same keys and access as our trusted tools, so it can read and send away sensitive data.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Isolate dynamically installed MCP servers with least privilege",
        "given": "an MCP server was installed at runtime",
        "when": "the agent invokes it",
        "then": "it runs in a sandbox with no access to agent credentials or secret environment, with egress limited to an explicit allowlist and only the minimum arguments it needs"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "Spoofing",
      "title": "Registry or download channel is impersonated to deliver a substituted MCP server",
      "scenario": "An attacker who can poison DNS, sit on the network path, or compromise a registry mirror serves a different artifact than the one the agent intended to install. Since the design relies on a public registry at runtime with no stated verification, the agent installs and trusts the substituted server.",
      "component": "Agent runtime <-> public MCP registry channel",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 5,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "discover and install new MCP servers from a public registry at runtime" }
      ],
      "asvs": [],
      "cwe": ["CWE-345", "CWE-494"],
      "plainLanguage": "Someone could pretend to be the tool catalogue and hand the agent a fake tool instead.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Authenticate the registry and pin artifacts",
        "given": "the agent resolves an MCP server from the registry",
        "when": "it fetches the artifact",
        "then": "the connection is mutually authenticated over TLS to a pinned host and the artifact digest matches a pinned value or publisher signature, otherwise the install fails closed"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "ElevationOfPrivilege",
      "title": "No authorisation gate on who or what can trigger a tool install",
      "scenario": "Deterministic signals report exposure public and auth false. Any caller who can reach the agent, or any prompt it processes, can make it install an arbitrary MCP server and thereby extend its own capabilities. This turns a user-level request into the ability to add new privileged tools (ASI03).",
      "component": "MCP tool discovery/install component",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 5,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "\"exposure\":\"public\",\"llmFeatures\":true,\"fileUpload\":false,\"auth\":false" },
        { "quote": "so it can use new tools without a deploy" }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V8.1.1"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-306", "CWE-862"],
      "plainLanguage": "Right now anyone who can talk to the agent can make it add new tools for itself.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Require authenticated, authorised approval for tool installation",
        "given": "a request or model decision asks to install a new MCP server",
        "when": "the install endpoint is called",
        "then": "the caller is authenticated, holds an explicit tool-admin permission, and a human approval step is recorded before the server becomes available"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "Tampering",
      "title": "A previously approved MCP server is updated to a malicious version",
      "scenario": "Runtime installation means the agent picks up whatever version the registry currently serves. An attacker who compromises a maintainer account ships a backdoored release; the agent installs it on the next discovery with no review, bypassing the normal deploy gate (ASI04 agentic supply chain).",
      "component": "MCP tool discovery/install component",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 5,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "install new MCP servers from a public registry at runtime so it can use new tools without a deploy" }
      ],
      "asvs": [],
      "cwe": ["CWE-1357", "CWE-494"],
      "plainLanguage": "A tool we trusted yesterday can silently change into a malicious one today because there is no version lock.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Pin and re-review MCP server versions",
        "given": "an MCP server is already approved",
        "when": "the registry offers a different version",
        "then": "the agent keeps the pinned version and the new version is only used after signature verification and a recorded re-approval"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "DenialOfService",
      "title": "Unbounded runtime installs exhaust the agent host",
      "scenario": "Because installs are triggered at runtime without a deploy gate, an attacker (or a looping agent) requests many large or hostile MCP servers, consuming disk, CPU and network, or installs a server that hangs tool calls. The agent becomes unavailable, and failures cascade to every workflow that depends on it (ASI08).",
      "component": "MCP client runtime",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "can discover and install new MCP servers from a public registry at runtime" }
      ],
      "asvs": [],
      "cwe": ["CWE-770", "CWE-400"],
      "plainLanguage": "Someone could make the agent install endless tools until it runs out of space or hangs.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Bound installs and tool execution",
        "given": "install or tool-invocation requests arrive",
        "when": "counts, artifact size, or execution time exceed configured limits",
        "then": "the request is rejected, the tool call is timed out, and the agent continues serving existing workflows"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "Repudiation",
      "title": "No record of which tool version acted, so harmful agent actions cannot be traced",
      "scenario": "Tools appear and change at runtime without a deploy record. After a damaging action it is impossible to establish which MCP server, version and publisher the agent used, letting an attacker's malicious tool remain unidentified and blocking incident response or rollback.",
      "component": "Installed MCP server packages/config",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "so it can use new tools without a deploy" }
      ],
      "asvs": [],
      "cwe": ["CWE-778"],
      "plainLanguage": "Because tools change by themselves, we cannot tell afterwards which tool did something bad.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Record an immutable inventory of installed tools and invocations",
        "given": "an MCP server is installed or invoked",
        "when": "the event occurs",
        "then": "the server name, source, version digest, approver and each invocation's arguments summary are written to tamper-evident storage retrievable during incident response"
      }
    }
  ]
}
